title: Identity transitions and the canonical derived tensor unit
statement:
The actual derived identity transition at a coefficient level is the inverse canonical comparison of identity-coefficient restriction with the identity derived functor. Its transpose under the scalar derived adjunction is exactly the canonical tensor unit of the constructed tensor coherence.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
variable [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
theorem systemDerivedTransition_tensorUnit
    (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (n : ℕ)
    (M : DerivedCategory (StrictRingSystem B)) :
    ((systemDerivedTensorAdj S B (Nat.le_refl n)).homEquiv _ _).symm
      ((systemDerivedTransition B (Nat.le_refl n)).app M) =
    ((systemTensorCoherence S).derivedUnit B n).hom.app ((derivedSystemEvaluation B n).obj M)
```

proof.text: Localize the strict identity law and cancel the exact target factors. The inverse restriction unit factorization gives the identity transition formula. The canonical derived tensor unit is the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism against the identity adjunction; its normalized Hom formula says its transpose becomes identity after the restriction comparison. Cancel that comparison.
